fact: Tech Africa News reported on 2026-08-14 that the DRC, through its Universal Service Development Fund (FDSU), is developing a national strategy to expand mobile and broadband connectivity in underserved areas, and the document gives no adoption and no period.
system: national strategy to expand mobile coverage (FDSU)

fact: Developing Telecoms reported on 2026-08-13 that the FDSU unveiled a National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035 with a 2030 target of 3,000 localities and 16 million people, and that further consultations with stakeholders are planned as it is refined; no government adoption is stated.

The FDSU signed subsidy agreements with Airtel, Orange, Vodacom and Africell for 10 localities each (40 localities, about 258,000 people) as the first step of the National Connectivity Strategy 2026-2035, per Developing Telecoms citing Ecofin; published 2026-08-13, signing date not given.

The FDSU's own microsite, dated by proxy to 2026-08 (published date used), says the FDSU is implementing a national universal-connectivity strategy, with a 40-site phase 0 and a phase 1 of about 300 sites in five zones; the page gives no period.
system: Stratégie Nationale pour la Connectivité Universelle
